plan.title: Pinned AGENTS rule names deft scm:body:* but the verbs are Taskfile-only; unknown-verb hint recommends the failing form; no rule-to-verb parity check

narratives.Description: Pinned AGENTS rule names deft scm:body:* but the verbs are Taskfile-only; unknown-verb hint recommends the failing form; no rule-to-verb parity check
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

The `scm:body:*` family (issue fetch, issue edit, issue create, comment create, comment edit, PR edit, body lints) has shipped since v0.89.0 (#1555, #2607, #2960) as **Taskfile tasks** in `tasks/scm.yml`, backed by `packages/core/src/intake/github-body-cli.ts`. It is **not registered in the `deft` CLI router** on any engine: the global `@deftai/directive@0.123.0` and the HEAD build both answer `unknown verb 'scm:body:issue:fetch'`.

The rules disagree on which form to use:

- The **always-pinned rule** in the managed `AGENTS.md` section ("Windows PowerShell: multi-line git/gh bodies (#2646 / #2744)") and its source `content/templates/agents-entry.md` prescribe `deft scm:body:* --body-file` and `deft scm:body:issue:fetch --out-file` then `deft scm:body:issue:edit --body-file`. That form resolves on no engine.
- The depth doc `content/scm/github.md` prescribes `task scm:body:*` with worked examples. That form works.
- The CLI unknown-verb hint (`packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts`, "Hyphen stem" message) suggests "try `deft scm:body:issue:fetch` (CLI)", the command that just failed, plus a hyphen stem that is equally unregistered.
- No check verifies that `deft <verb>` names in the pinned rules resolve in the router, or that `task <name>` names resolve in the Taskfile. The only verb gate in the release path (`closed-verb-gate`) is about publish authorisation.

## Effect

An agent that reads only the pinned rule (the point of pinning) runs a dead command, gets a hint pointing back at it, and improvises with raw `gh`. That is the #2744 PowerShell body-mangling footgun the rule exists to prevent. Observed 2026-10-09 while editing #5514; recovered with a guarded `gh` fallback. The `task` form was the correct move and the pinned rule did not name it.

## Fix

1. **Register the `scm:body:*` family in the CLI router** (dual-invoke parity with `task scm:body:*`) so the pinned rule is true as written and consumers without go-task have a path. After #5490 (consumer-only self-hosting, #5514) the CLI form is the one that works for every consumer.
2. **Unknown-verb hint:** never recommend the form that just failed. When a Taskfile task of the same name exists, say `task <name> -- ...` (framework) / `task deft:<name> -- ...` (consumer include).
3. **Rule-to-verb parity check** as a new verify wired into `deft check`: every `deft <verb>` named in `content/templates/agents-entry.md` and `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` resolves in the router; every `task <name>` named there resolves in the Taskfile. Fail closed.
4. Until 1 lands, or if 1 is rejected: change the two pinned-rule lines to the Taskfile form to match `scm/github.md`, and run `task agents:refresh` (#1309 propagation).

## Acceptance

- `deft scm:body:issue:fetch --repo OWNER/NAME --issue N --out-file <path>` and `deft scm:body:issue:edit --repo OWNER/NAME --issue N --body-file <path>` work on the released CLI with the same fail-closed live read-back as the `task` form; same for the comment and PR verbs.
- `deft <unregistered>` never suggests the same unregistered spelling; it suggests the `task` form when one exists.
- The new verify fails on a template that names an unregistered `deft` verb and passes on the current templates after the fix.
- The pinned `AGENTS.md` rule, `agents-entry.md`, and `scm/github.md` agree on the invocation form.

## Why urgent

An always-pinned, consumer-facing rule prescribes a dead command on the one path (win32 issue-body read-modify-write) where improvising corrupts bodies.

Refs: #2646, #2744, #2607, #1555, #2960, #5514, #5490.
